feat(collector): a watch and a period refresh a session's transcript lanes, and a request waits on its world state (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.zhh) (#760)

* feat(collector): a watch and a period refresh a session's transcript lanes, and a request waits on its world state (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.zhh)

One keyed entry per followed session reads every transcript lane (session,
speed, context, metrics, activity, cache, auto-compact). A watch on the
transcript and on Claude Code's settings file reads them again after a write,
and a 10 s backstop period catches a dropped event. A request is no longer a
trigger: it waits only for its world state's first readings, so a warm
session draws at once.

- Each lane's owner records its refresh under the trigger that caused it
  (first, period, change), and every refresh writes its own line, so a lane
  that never lands is the one whose line is missing.
- `request` leaves the refresh triggers; the render event's `refreshed=` field,
  the adapter's refresh reach and RefreshTimes are gone.
- Speed takes a sample only when the transcript's stamp moved.
- `today` leaves the transcript lanes: its fault is the session lane's.

* fix(collector): a change heard while nobody holds an entry is read when its hold returns, and transcript holds show in stats (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.zhh)

- A keyed entry owes one re-read for a change heard since its stored read
  began; it runs once the entry is held and no read is out, so a session back
  from idle draws the write it missed instead of waiting out its period.
- The stats snapshot lists the transcript lanes' held entries.
- The demo closes the transcript lanes with the other providers.
- SOURCES-AND-FRAMES no longer names a request as a refresh trigger.

* fix(speed): tok/s is a projection of the draw's instant, so an idle session's rate ends (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.zhh)

A sample is taken only when the transcript's stamp moves, so nothing ended the
last turn's rate once a session went idle: the bar kept it for hours. The rate
is now drawn against the draw's own instant, like today, and ends a sample
window after the last sample; the burn-rate history stays.

* fix(ledger): a session lane's refresh is a step of its transcript entry's, which is the one line (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.zhh)

- A source declares whether its refresh is a unit of work (its own line) or a
  step of another's (a line only when it fails, still counted). The session
  lanes are steps of their transcript entry's refresh, so a write costs one
  line, and a session with no transcript yet one per period, not six.
- Every draw, the demo's and check's included, projects today and speed
  through one function, so the demo draws tok/s again.
- The watch key is the entry's key; the awaited built-ins are listed once.

* test(e2e): a render that timed out on every attempt names what the daemon logged meanwhile (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.zhh)

* test(daemon-value): a timer left over after close is shown with the daemon's log (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.zhh)

* fix(providers): one close ends every provider, so no rig leaves a transcript period re-arming (candybar-skeleton-wj0c.zhh)

The daemon, the demo and two test rigs each listed the providers to close by hand, and the lists drifted when the transcript lanes arrived: an entry still held keeps its 10 s period re-arming for the life of the jest worker, which another file's close-ends-everything ledger then counts. The providers' own close is now the one list; the rigs that build a transcript trigger of their own close it, and a test's holds close with it.
